GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2015-02-26T06:41:20Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Question, how to make a variable within declared module name
Description: I am writing a test and I have an issue.
The test runner doesn't have the global object I need since it is running in a different environment.
I want to create this object because strict mode complains otherwise, but TypeScript cannot do it.

I have declaration:

``` typescript
declare module Q {
    function f(): string;
}
```

and usage

``` typescript
var x = Q.f();
```

Now in my test I want to mock Q.f and create object of my own.

``` typescript
var Q = { ... }
```

The TypeScript complains about multiple declarations.

There is a workaround to access the module through the global 'window' object in the code and then it is possible to test it.

``` typescript
interface Window {
 Q: QInterface;
}

interface QInterface {
    function f(): string;
}

// the code
var x = !!window.Q ? window.Q.f() : "";
```

I would like to not use the workaround and find some solution without changing my code.
Thanks.
